title: Make authored clients and proxy adapters accepted by the server
goal: Repair outbound HTTP framing and remove connection-specific headers when a custom client or proxy receives stricter Kestrel protocol failures.

runtime.reason: Actual .NET 11 RC2 execution, not GA verification.
runtime.name: .NET

language.reason: Explicit sample language mode; .NET 10 comparison uses C# 14. No experimental language feature.
language.name: C#

packageAssets: Microsoft.AspNetCore.App net11.0 and System.Net.Quic runtime/native MsQuic assets; no added NuGet dependency. Older comparison uses corresponding net10.0 assets.
providers: Kestrel loopback server; no database or external resource provider.
platforms: ASP.NET Core supported server platforms. HTTP/3 execution additionally requires System.Net.Quic/MsQuic, supported OS TLS 1.3, UDP loopback access and QUIC support. Actual Windows x64 with msquic.dll 2.5.11.159415436; no cross-platform execution claim.
renderingModes: Server HTTP endpoints; no Blazor rendering mode.
prerequisites: Use a separate directory for each complete sample below, retaining its SDK/project/package boundary. Restore required packs/packages before the sample runs. Installed Playbook guidance itself is fully offline.
Fixtures bind ephemeral loopback ports and stop their hosts. Certificates are temporary and are not added to shared trust stores.
constraints: Correct the emitting client or proxy, not a fabricated server compatibility switch. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 prohibit connection-specific headers except TE: trailers; remove Connection-nominated fields and regenerate outbound authority/framing. HTTP/1.1 CL+TE is processed then closed, not categorically rejected; closure is also serviced to older supported releases.
stabilityLimitations: Stable API intent for .NET 11, verified with RC2 under ADR 0004. Final GA reconciliation remains pending; RC2 differences are disclosed in the body.

sources.title: Official ASP.NET Core 11 capability and migration reference

evidence.scope: Actual TCP HTTP/1.1 ambiguous framing closes after response; corrected requests reuse the connection. Raw HPACK HTTP/2 and QPACK HTTP/3 send six malformed/corrected pairs each. RC2 rejects all six; .NET 10.0.13 accepts four obsolete headers and rejects Connection/invalid TE. Corrected requests receive OK. Request counters exclude accidental application acceptance; MsQuic 2.5.11.159415436 used on Windows x64.
